_note: Engine knowledge base — how events transmit to MCX and who in India gets hit. Load into article/geo prompts for precise, institutional-quality writing.

mechanism.crude: Hormuz Strait carries ~20% of global seaborne oil (17–20 mb/d). Any credible blockade risk adds a war premium of $5–15/bbl to WTI/Brent within hours. MCX crude amplifies this by USD/INR — every $1/bbl on WTI = ~₹130–160/bbl on MCX at current exchange rates.
mechanism.gold: Classic safe-haven bid. Past Iran escalations drove gold +2–4% in the first 48 hours before fading as premiums compress. Silver moves in sympathy but with higher volatility.

india_affected.aviation: IndiGo, Air India, SpiceJet, Akasa — ATF (aviation turbine fuel) is revised fortnightly by OMCs. A $10/bbl move in crude = ~₹6–8/litre ATF cost change. Unhedged carriers face direct margin pressure within 15 days.
india_affected.omcs: BPCL, HPCL, Indian Oil — under-recovery risk if retail petrol/diesel prices are not revised to match crude. Government often absorbs short-term spikes; sustained move above $95 Brent for 10+ days typically triggers a retail price revision.
india_affected.paint: Asian Paints, Berger Paints, Kansai Nerolac — solvents (toluene, xylene) and titanium dioxide feedstocks are crude derivatives. A 5% crude spike adds ~1–2% raw material cost within one procurement cycle (45–60 days).
india_affected.petrochemicals: Reliance Industries, HPCL-Mittal Energy, GAIL — naphtha and LPG feedstock costs rise directly with crude. Downstream polymer margins compress.
india_affected.fertilisers: Coromandel International, Chambal Fertilisers — urea and DAP use natural gas as feedstock; crude spikes often drag natgas higher. Import cost of phosphatic fertilisers rises.
india_affected.logistics: Blue Dart, Delhivery, VRL Logistics — diesel costs (which track crude with a lag) feed directly into per-km operating costs. Freight rate revisions typically lag 30–60 days.
india_affected.tyres: MRF, Apollo Tyres, CEAT — natural rubber is unaffected but synthetic rubber (SBR, PBR) is a crude derivative. A sustained crude spike adds to input costs within one quarter.

iran_israel_escalation.historical_moves: Oct 2023 (Hamas attack): WTI +4.3% intraday, MCX Crude +4.8%, reversed 60% within 5 sessions. Apr 2024 (Iran drone strike): WTI +3.1%, gold +1.8%, both reversed within 72h on no escalation. Jun 2025 (naval incident): crude +2.8%, faded same session. Pattern: initial spike of 3–8% fades within 3–5 sessions if Hormuz remains open.
iran_israel_escalation.reversal_trigger: Confirmed ceasefire, US diplomatic mediation announcement, or IAEA-verified Iran nuclear compliance signal.
iran_israel_escalation.escalation_trigger: Confirmed Hormuz tanker seizure, Iranian port blockade, or Israeli strike on Iranian oil infrastructure.

mechanism.crude: OPEC+ collectively controls ~40% of global oil supply. A 500k bpd cut tightens the market by ~0.5% of global demand (~100 mb/d). Price impact depends on pre-existing inventory levels — cuts during inventory draws amplify; cuts during builds are partially offset. Typical initial WTI move: +2–5% on surprise cuts, +1–2% on telegraphed cuts.

india_affected.omcs: BPCL, HPCL, Indian Oil — India imports ~85% of crude needs. Higher crude = higher import bill. Every $10/bbl sustained rise costs India ~$15bn/year in additional import costs, widening the current account deficit.
india_affected.refining_margins: Reliance (GRM) — tighter crude supply historically improves gross refining margins for complex refiners who can process heavier grades that widen in discount. Simple refiners face margin compression.
india_affected.aviation: Same as Iran scenario — ATF cost pressure with 15-day revision lag.
india_affected.steel: JSW Steel, Tata Steel — coking coal logistics and energy costs rise; marginal impact compared to direct crude users but present in energy-intensive steelmaking.

opec_production_cut.historical_moves: Nov 2022 OPEC+ 2mb/d cut: WTI +8% over 3 sessions. Apr 2023 surprise 1.16mb/d cut: WTI +6.3% in one session. Oct 2023 extended cuts: WTI +3.2%. Pattern: surprise cuts move market 4–8%; pre-signalled cuts move 1–3%.
opec_production_cut.reversal_trigger: US SPR release announcement, surprise inventory build >4mb EIA, or Saudi Arabia signalling quota relaxation.
opec_production_cut.key_data: OPEC+ meets every 2 months. Saudi Aramco official selling price (OSP) for Asia, released first week of each month, is the real-time signal of Saudi supply intent.

mechanism.crude: Opposite of cut. 400–500k bpd increase = ~0.4–0.5% of global supply addition. Market impact softened if demand outlook is strong. Typical WTI move: -2–5% on surprise increases.

india_affected.omcs: Relief for BPCL, HPCL, IOC — lower crude = lower import costs = under-recovery narrows. Government saves on LPG and kerosene subsidies.
india_affected.aviation: IndiGo, Air India — ATF cost reduction with 15-day lag. Margin relief for unhedged carriers.
india_affected.consumers: Retail petrol/diesel price reduction likely within one fortnightly revision cycle if crude sustains below key levels.

opec_production_increase.historical_moves: Jun 2023 OPEC+ surprise increase: WTI -5.2% in one session. Aug 2022 token 100k bpd increase: minimal price impact (-0.8%) — market read it as cover for actual flat output.
opec_production_increase.reversal_trigger: Geopolitical flare-up, demand surge from China, or EIA draw >3mb.

mechanism.crude: Russia produces ~9–10 mb/d. Western sanctions and price caps affect ~1–1.5 mb/d of flow routing. Escalation raises re-routing risk and tightens European energy markets.
mechanism.natgas: Russia supplied ~35% of European gas pre-2022. Disruptions to Nord Stream (now offline), TurkStream, or Ukrainian transit routes spike European TTF gas, which drives LNG demand globally and lifts Henry Hub by correlation.
mechanism.gold: War escalation consistently drives gold safe-haven demand. Ukraine-Russia conflict correlation with gold: +0.7 over 30-day windows during escalation phases.
mechanism.wheat: Ukraine + Russia = ~30% of global wheat exports. Port blockades at Odessa historically spike wheat futures 5–15% within 48h. India grows wheat domestically but global price sets the import parity floor.

india_affected.fertilisers: India imports ~60% of its potash from Belarus/Russia. Sanctions disruption raises DAP/MOP import costs — Coromandel, Chambal, IFFCO face input cost pressure.
india_affected.sunflower_oil: Ukraine supplies ~50% of global sunflower oil. Port disruptions spike edible oil prices — Adani Wilmar, Ruchi Soya face raw material cost pressure.
india_affected.steel: Ukraine is a major pig iron and semi-finished steel exporter. Disruptions tighten global scrap/billet supply — marginal tightening for Indian steelmakers.
india_affected.gas: India's LNG imports (primarily from Qatar and US) see demand competition from Europe scrambling for LNG. Spot LNG prices can spike 20–40% in acute disruption — GAIL, Petronet LNG face procurement cost pressure.

russia_ukraine_escalation.historical_moves: Feb 24 2022 invasion: WTI +8%, gold +2.7%, wheat futures +15% in one session. Oct 2022 escalation: crude +2.1%, gold +1.3%. Pattern: initial spike fades within 5–10 sessions unless supply is physically disrupted.
russia_ukraine_escalation.reversal_trigger: Ceasefire talks, US/EU mediation, grain corridor agreement, or IAEA nuclear facility safety confirmation.

mechanism.crude: Suez Canal handles ~10% of global seaborne oil (and ~30% of container trade). Rerouting via Cape of Good Hope adds 10–14 days and $1–3mn per voyage in fuel/time costs. This creates a physical tightening of ~500k–1mb/d equivalent, pushing freight rates (VLCC) and crude spot premiums higher.

india_affected.textile: India is a major textile exporter to Europe. Rerouting adds 10–14 days and 20–30% to freight costs — Arvind Ltd, Welspun, KPR Mill face margin compression.
india_affected.electronics: Consumer electronics imports from Europe routed via Suez face delays — Dixon Technologies (contract manufacturer) supply chain disruption.
india_affected.crude_importers: BPCL, HPCL, Reliance — freight premium on crude imports from Middle East loaded on Suezmax tankers rises $1–2/bbl.
india_affected.gems_jewellery: Diamond rough imports from Antwerp route via Suez — rerouting costs add to import lead times.

red_sea_suez_disruption.historical_moves: Nov 2023 Houthi attacks: VLCC freight rates +40% in 3 weeks, Brent +2.1%. Jan 2024 full rerouting: Brent premium +$3–4/bbl sustained. Pattern: price impact is gradual (weeks) not immediate (hours) unless tanker is directly attacked.
red_sea_suez_disruption.reversal_trigger: US/coalition naval escort programme, Houthi ceasefire, or Yemen political resolution.

mechanism.gold: Higher US rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold. Dollar strengthens, gold falls. Rule of thumb: 25bps surprise hike = gold -0.8 to -1.5%.
mechanism.silver: Dual sensitivity — safe-haven (like gold, falls with rate hike) and industrial (falls with slower growth expectations). Typically falls more than gold on hikes.
mechanism.copper: Rate hikes signal slower growth → lower industrial demand → copper falls. China demand offset is the key variable.
mechanism.crude: Dollar strengthening from rate hikes makes dollar-priced crude more expensive for non-US buyers, dampening demand. Secondary effect via growth slowdown expectations.

india_affected.jewellers: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, Senco Gold — lower gold prices reduce inventory mark-to-market but also soften consumer buying sentiment (expecting further falls).
india_affected.gold_importers: India imports ~800–1000 tonnes/year. Lower gold = lower import bill = CAD relief. Every $100/oz fall saves India ~$3–4bn/year.
india_affected.rupee: Fed hike typically strengthens dollar → rupee weakens → ALL MCX prices higher in INR even if USD price falls. Net effect on MCX gold is often muted or positive in INR terms.
india_affected.nbfcs: Gold loan NBFCs (Muthoot Finance, Manappuram) — collateral values fall, LTV buffers compress if gold falls >10% from pledged levels.

fed_rate_hike.historical_moves: Mar 2022 first hike: gold -0.9% on day, rallied +4% over next month (war risk offset). Jun 2022 75bps hike: gold -1.7% on day. Aug 2023 Jackson Hole hawkish: gold -1.4%, silver -2.1%. Pattern: initial negative reaction, recovery if real rates plateau.
fed_rate_hike.reversal_trigger: Fed pivot signal, pause language, softer CPI print, or weak NFP.

mechanism.gold: Lower rates reduce opportunity cost of gold. Dollar weakens, gold rises. Rule of thumb: 25bps surprise cut = gold +0.8 to +2%.
mechanism.silver: Benefits doubly — safe-haven and industrial demand both supported by easing.
mechanism.copper: Lower rates support growth expectations → industrial demand → copper rises.
mechanism.crude: Weaker dollar makes crude cheaper in non-USD currencies, supporting demand.

india_affected.jewellers: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers — gold rally typically boosts wedding season buying and investment demand.
india_affected.gold_etfs: SGB (Sovereign Gold Bond) redemptions accelerate when gold rallies. Nippon India Gold ETF, HDFC Gold ETF see inflows.
india_affected.rupee: Dollar weakens → rupee strengthens → MCX prices partially offset despite USD commodity rally. Net effect: MCX gold rises but less than COMEX.

fed_rate_cut.historical_moves: Sep 2024 50bps cut: gold +1.2% same day, +3.8% over week. Nov 2023 pause-then-pivot: gold +4.1% in 2 weeks.
fed_rate_cut.reversal_trigger: Hotter-than-expected CPI, strong NFP, or Fed re-signalling higher for longer.

mechanism.copper: China consumes ~55% of global refined copper. PMI below 50 signals contraction in manufacturing activity. Rule of thumb: PMI miss of 1 point = copper -0.8 to -1.5% on day.
mechanism.crude: China is the world's largest crude importer (~11 mb/d). Demand growth assumptions drive futures premium. Weak PMI cuts demand growth forecasts — crude falls 1–3% on significant miss.
mechanism.silver: Industrial demand (solar panels, electronics) falls with China slowdown. Silver underperforms gold when China PMI weakens.

india_affected.copper: Hindalco (copper smelter), Sterlite Copper — LME copper price sets benchmark for MCX; lower copper = lower realisation.
india_affected.steel: JSW, Tata Steel — China oversupply risk rises when domestic demand weakens, as excess steel floods export markets and depresses global prices.
india_affected.zinc_aluminium: Hindustan Zinc, Nalco — same dynamic as copper.

china_pmi_weak.historical_moves: Aug 2023 weak Caixin PMI: copper -2.3%, crude -1.8%. Apr 2024 PMI miss: copper -1.1%. Pattern: sharp same-day reaction, often partially recovered within 48h.
china_pmi_weak.reversal_trigger: China stimulus announcement, PBoC rate cut, or strong exports data offsetting PMI weakness.

mechanism.gold: RBI rate hold or cut → rupee pressure → MCX gold rises in INR even if COMEX flat. RBI hike → rupee firms → MCX gold falls in INR even if COMEX flat.
mechanism.rupee: RBI is the primary driver of USD/INR. Surprise cuts weaken rupee 0.3–0.8% on day; surprise hikes firm rupee 0.2–0.6%.

india_affected.gold_importers: India's jewellery industry (Titan, Kalyan) — MCX gold price is the direct reference for domestic gold retail pricing. RBI action changes MCX more than COMEX.
india_affected.importers: All commodity importers face rupee transmission — crude, edible oils, fertilisers, copper all priced in dollars. Weaker rupee = higher INR landed cost.
india_affected.exporters: IT companies, pharma — benefit from weaker rupee. Not commodity relevant directly but drives macro flows.

india_rbi_policy.historical_moves: Feb 2023 surprise 25bps hike: rupee +0.4%, MCX gold -0.7% same day. Apr 2023 pause: rupee flat, MCX gold +0.2%.
india_rbi_policy.reversal_trigger: Inflation data surprise, foreign capital outflows, or global dollar move overriding RBI action.

mechanism.gold: India's basic customs duty on gold is currently 15% (6% basic + 5% AIDC + 4% IGST approximate). Each 1% BCD change = ~₹1,500–1,800/10g change in domestic MCX price relative to international parity. Duty cuts immediately reduce MCX gold vs COMEX spread.
mechanism.silver: Similar duty structure. 1% duty change = ~₹2,000–2,500/kg impact on MCX silver.
mechanism.copper: Lower duty for raw copper ore vs refined copper — changes affect domestic pricing of Hindalco's secondary copper.

india_affected.jewellers: Titan, Kalyan, PC Jeweller — duty cuts reduce gold purchase cost, improve margins; duty hikes squeeze margins or force price increases reducing volume.
india_affected.smuggling: High duty historically increases smuggling — DGRI/DRI seizure data is a lagging indicator of duty arbitrage.
india_affected.recycling: Domestic gold recycling volumes rise when imports become expensive (high duty); fall when imports are cheap.
india_affected.importers: MMTC, STC, authorised bank importers — duty changes affect their import economics directly.

india_import_duty_change.historical_moves: Jul 2024 BCD cut from 15% to 6%: MCX gold fell ₹4,000–5,000/10g same day (largest single-day drop in years). Jul 2022 BCD hike from 10.75% to 15%: MCX gold rose ₹1,500/10g above international parity.
india_import_duty_change.reversal_trigger: Duty cuts are typically permanent until next budget. Hikes may be partially reversed if CAD widens.

mechanism.crude: EIA weekly petroleum status report (Wednesday 8 PM IST). Draw = inventory fell = supply tighter than demand. Significant draw >3mb/week = bullish. Cushing OK hub draws get more weight than total US inventories. Rule of thumb: 3mb draw surprise = WTI +0.8 to +1.5%.

india_affected.omcs: BPCL, HPCL, IOC — inventory-driven crude rally sustains import cost pressure. Short-term price setter for OMC procurement hedging.
india_affected.refining: Reliance Industries — GRM (gross refining margin) is sensitive to crude-product spread. Inventory draws that raise crude faster than product prices temporarily compress GRM.

eia_crude_draw.historical_moves: Aug 2023 -17mb surprise draw: WTI +2.3% in session. Feb 2024 -7mb: WTI +1.1%. Pattern: draws >5mb are reliably bullish; draws 1–3mb are noise.
eia_crude_draw.reversal_trigger: Consecutive builds, SPR refill announcement, or demand destruction evidence.

mechanism.crude: Build = inventory rose = supply exceeding demand. Significant build >3mb/week = bearish. Consecutive builds historically signal demand weakness or supply glut. Rule of thumb: 3mb build surprise = WTI -0.8 to -1.5%.

india_affected.omcs: BPCL, HPCL, IOC — lower crude costs reduce import bill; potential for downstream fuel price reduction. OMC refining margins may improve as product prices hold while crude falls.
india_affected.consumers: Petrol/diesel price revision (fortnightly) becomes more likely if builds persist and crude falls >$5 from last revision baseline.

eia_crude_build.historical_moves: Jun 2023 +7mb build: WTI -3.4% in session. Oct 2022 +9.9mb: WTI -2.1%. Pattern: large surprise builds (>5mb) reliably bearish; smaller builds absorbed.
eia_crude_build.reversal_trigger: OPEC+ supply discipline re-affirmation, geopolitical risk premium, or China demand revival signal.

crude.mcx_contract: MCX Crude Oil — NYMEX WTI-linked. Lot size: 100 barrels. Pricing in ₹/barrel.
crude.india_import_dependency: India imports ~85% of crude requirements (~5 mb/d). Second-largest crude importer after China.
crude.transmission: WTI $1/bbl move = MCX ₹130–160/bbl at USD/INR 84–86. USD/INR amplifies or dampens the move.
crude.major_producers: Saudi Arabia, Russia, USA, UAE, Iraq. OPEC+ collectively ~40% of global supply.
crude.india_price_mechanism: Retail petrol/diesel revised fortnightly by OMCs (Indian Oil, BPCL, HPCL) based on 15-day rolling average of benchmark crude + exchange rate.

gold.mcx_contract: MCX Gold — COMEX-linked. Lot size: 1 kg (Gold Mini: 100g). Pricing in ₹/10g.
gold.india_demand: India is world's second-largest gold consumer (~800–1000 tonnes/year). ~60% jewellery, ~25% investment, ~15% industrial.
gold.transmission: COMEX $1/oz move = MCX ~₹2.7/10g at current rates. Import duty (currently ~15%) creates a domestic premium above import parity.
gold.seasonal_pattern: Akha Teej (Apr-May), Dhanteras (Oct-Nov), wedding season (Nov-Dec, Feb-Apr) = peak physical demand. Lean season: Jan-Feb, Jun-Sep.
gold.india_price_mechanism: MCX gold = COMEX gold × USD/INR × import duty factor × GST. Hallmarking mandatory since 2022 for all retail gold.

silver.mcx_contract: MCX Silver — COMEX-linked. Lot size: 30 kg. Pricing in ₹/kg.
silver.india_demand: India imports ~6,000–8,000 tonnes/year. Largest single-country silver importer globally. Used in solar panels, electronics, jewellery.
silver.transmission: Dual driver — gold moves (safe haven) AND industrial demand (China PMI, solar installations). Silver more volatile than gold: gold:silver volatility ratio ~1:1.7.
silver.unique_india_factor: India's solar mission (500 GW by 2030) is a structural demand driver. Every GW of solar requires ~1.5 tonnes of silver for photovoltaic cells.

copper.mcx_contract: MCX Copper — LME-linked. Lot size: 1 tonne. Pricing in ₹/kg.
copper.india_context: India produces ~750,000 tonnes/year (Hindalco + Vedanta). Net importer of refined copper. Major user: power cables, telecom, EVs.
copper.transmission: LME copper drives MCX copper. China 55% of global demand — China PMI is the primary driver.
copper.india_growth_driver: India's power sector capex (PGCIL, state DISCOMs) and EV adoption are structural demand drivers. Each EV uses 4× more copper than ICE vehicle.

natgas.mcx_contract: MCX Natural Gas — Henry Hub-linked. Lot size: 1,250 mmBtu. Pricing in ₹/mmBtu.
natgas.india_context: India is a growing LNG importer. Domestic gas prices are partially deregulated. Key users: fertiliser plants, power generation, CGD (city gas distribution).
natgas.transmission: Henry Hub drives MCX NatGas. European TTF and JKM (Japan/Korea marker) diverge during supply crunches and pull LNG spot prices.
natgas.india_specific: GAIL, Petronet LNG, IGL, MGL are key domestic gas distributors. CNG prices (auto sector) and PNG prices (households) track domestic gas price revisions.
